concept.name: Price-time priority
concept.definition: The order-matching rule under which orders at a better price execute first, and among orders at the same price the earliest-submitted order executes first. CME Group's FIFO algorithm uses price and time as the only criteria for filling an order.
concept.intuition: You earn execution priority by offering a better price or by getting in line earlier.
concept.mechanics: Resting orders are ranked by price and then by timestamp; an incoming order fills against the front of the queue until exhausted. An order loses its time priority and is re-queued if its price is changed, its quantity is increased, or its account number is changed.
concept.failure_modes: It rewards speed, fueling latency arms races to reach the front of the queue, and it gives no extra share to large displayed size, which can discourage posting size. Under one-tick spreads, time priority dominates and queues grow long.
concept.misconceptions: Being first at a price guarantees fills only up to your order's size against incoming flow; it does not protect against the price moving away before any aggressor arrives.
concept.example: A 3-lot bid entered at 14:47 and a 5-lot bid at 15:05, both at 9330: under FIFO the 3-lot matches first when a seller arrives.

citations.source: CME Group Client Systems Wiki, 'Supported Matching Algorithms'
